sections.heading: Stem changes in -ir verbs
sections.body: *-ar* and *-er* verbs never change their stem in the preterite. But *-ir* verbs that change in the present (*pedir, dormir, preferir…*) also change in the preterite — only in the third person (*él, ella, usted, ellos, ellas, ustedes*): e → i, o → u.

sections.heading: More verbs like these
sections.body: e → i: *repetir* (*repitió*), *servir* (*sirvió*), *seguir* (*siguió*), *sentir* (*sintió*), *vestirse* (*se vistió*), *divertirse* (*se divirtió* — had fun). o → u: *morir* (*murió* — died).

sections.heading: Telling a story in order
sections.body:
Link completed events with sequence words: *primero* (first), *luego / después* (then), *más tarde* (later), *entonces* (so, then), *al final / por fin* (finally, at last). And set the scene in time: *un día* (one day), *esa noche* (that night), *a las ocho* (at eight), *dos horas después* (two hours later).

*Primero fuimos al museo, luego comimos en el centro y al final volvimos al hotel.*

examples: She preferred to stay at home.
El mesero nos sirvió el vino.
The waiter served us the wine.
Nos divertimos mucho en la fiesta.
We had a lot of fun at the party.
They had a lot of fun.
First we went to the museum.
In the end we went back to the hotel.
Un día conocí a una chica en el tren.
One day I met a girl on the train.
Dos horas después, llegó la policía.
Two hours later, the police arrived.
At last I finished the book.
Siguieron la calle hasta el parque.
They followed the street to the park.
So we decided to go back.
Afterwards we went to the beach.

exercises.prompt: Which verbs change their stem in the preterite?
options: -ir verbs that change in the present, only in the third person
all stem-changing verbs, in all forms

exercises.prompt: Does *volver* change in the preterite (*él volvió*)?
options: No, -er verbs don't change in the preterite
